hook_text: One volt, ten milliamps. Two volts, twenty. Three volts, thirty. There is a law hiding in those numbers.
clip_script: Volts is the push, measured across. Amps is the flow, measured in the loop. Ohms is the opposition. A 100 ohm resistor: 1 volt gives 10 milliamps, 2 gives 20, 3 gives 30. Double the push, double the flow. Volts over amps is always 100. That is Ohm's law: V equals I times R, as long as nothing heats up. Three forms: want volts, multiply; want amps or ohms, divide. Convert milliamps to amps first. LED resistor: 4.5 volt battery, LED eats 2, so 2.5 across the resistor; for 10 milliamps that is 250 ohms. The kit's 470 gives 5 milliamps. Safe. Formula, numbers, unit, sense check.
visual_style: Whiteboard table of volts and milliamps growing in step; a straight line graph through zero; the V I R triangle; the LED resistor sum written out.
mood: Clear and steady, like a good maths teacher.
pacing: Three quantities, the pattern, the law, three forms, convert, LED sum, check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and calculate the resistor for a 2 volt LED at 15 milliamps on 6 volts.
